findings.reason: The Definition uses products in H⊗H and H⊗3 for multiplicativity and the weak-unit identities, but its declared suppliers do not define the tensor-product algebra structure. Schauenburg §4 uses this standard structure ([source](https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/86703)).

The statement's H-Mod morphisms and proof steps 1.1 and 1.3 use H-linear maps, but def-left-and-right-modules defines module actions, not module homomorphisms. Add def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel to deps/Facts, or state the map condition explicitly.

“An ordinary Hopf algebra with Φ=1 is a special case of both” is too broad under the repository's definitions: the ordinary Hopf definition permits a nonbijective antipode, while the quasi-Hopf definition requires bijective S. Nonbijective ordinary Hopf antipodes exist ([Takeuchi](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jmath1948/23/4/23_4_561/_pdf)); the assigned counterexample's step 2.1 also shows that for Φ=1 a quasi-antipode yields an ordinary antipode by conjugation. Qualify the claim to ordinary Hopf algebras with bijective antipode.

The remark uses “ordinary Hopf algebra” without a dependency path to its definition. Add def-hh-hopf-algebra-and-antipode as an explicit prerequisite; it supplies the convention that makes the qualification above necessary.

The monoidal-category definition requires a bifunctor, but the proof does not define the induced tensor map on H-linear morphisms or check that it respects the balancing relations. Add the map [v⊗w]↦[f(v)⊗g(w)] and verify balancing, H-linearity, identities, and composition; include the module-homomorphism supplier.
